name: fig-10
title: fig-10: Development
confidence_basis: Calibrated off Provisional (workbench 0.4.1). BASELINE (fig10-emergence): the place-graph rewrite is demonstrated, BUT — as the scientific review flags — attachment and ECM fire at SCHEDULED ticks (config attach_at/mature_at), so this is a software/behavioral demonstration of the reorganization structure, not an emergent decision, and there are no controls. MECHANISTIC VARIANT (fig10-mechanistic, scientific-review revision) makes attachment EMERGE from spatial state: six motile cells aggregate by local adhesion and the biofilm forms only once a quorum sits in proximity for several sustained ticks — so the formation TIME varies with adhesion strength (0.25→t7, 0.35→t6, 0.55→t5) and with density, which a wall clock cannot do. Matched-null controls isolate each arm (no adhesion ⇒ never forms; no ECM ⇒ forms then disperses), cell identity and biomass are preserved on reparenting, and the collective cohesion port is inert until organization. Held at Provisional overall because it is a reduced 2-D aggregation model in LATTICE units with didactic adhesion/ECM rates — not calibrated to measured adhesion forces, ECM secretion rates, or a named organism.
question: Is the paper's §Development figure (Fig development) executable -- can a runnable process-bigraph composite demonstrate, under test, that development is "a hierarchical reorganization where individual cells become part of a collective composite" rather than merely more cells? Concretely: does running the `fig10-emergence` composite turn a set of free motile bacteria (top-level place-graph siblings) into a nested biofilm microcolony that then secretes an extracellular matrix -- surface attachment, ECM secretion, growth of a structured community (caption a) realized as a genuine runtime place-graph rewrite (caption b)?
biological_summary:
This study is the runnable, toy-real backing for the paper's §Development figure (Fig development). The paper argues that once self-maintaining cellular interfaces exist, "cellular interfaces can become coupled strongly enough to sustain a collective one": cells joined through adhesion, signaling, and shared extracellular stores form structures such as biofilms "in which individual interfaces become embedded in a collective interface with its own shared state and constraints." Development, the paper stresses, "is not only repeated growth and division but a coordinated change in the space of possible couplings" -- a hierarchical reorganization, not just population growth.
The `fig10-emergence` composite makes exactly that claim executable. Its state is an environment `tree[node]` holding a surface and four free motile bacteria as top-level siblings (each with biomass and a `motile` marker). A single `BiofilmEmergence` process fires two event-driven place-graph rewrites over a 16-step run: at `attach_at = 6` an ATTACHMENT + AGGREGATION rewrite moves all four free cells out of the top level and re-parents them as children of a NEW `biofilm` collective node (switching them sessile); at `mature_at = 12` a MATURATION rewrite has the sessile community secrete `ecm_count = 3` extracellular-matrix nodes inside the biofilm. The run is deterministic (no RNG), so every count and timing below is an exact regression pin, reproduced run to run.
The measured trajectory reads directly as caption a's "surface attachment, ECM secretion, growth of structured communities" and caption b's "hierarchical reorganization where individual cells become part of a collective composite": four free planktonic cells hold dispersed through t=5, then at t=6 all four attach at once (free count 4 -> 0, biofilm-nested count 0 -> 4) as the biofilm collective node appears; the cells' place-graph depth jumps from 1 (direct children of env) to 2 (children of the biofilm), and they never return to the top level. ECM stays absent until maturation and then accumulates 1 -> 2 -> 3 nodes over t=12..14, only ever while the sessile community is present. The planktonic -> sessile -> matured arc is the figure's dynamics panel.
Two companion place-graph rewrites, exercised by the same fig-10 test suite, round out the paper's §Growth/division/development/evolution section that this figure sits in. A cell-cycle rewrite (`build_fig10_division`) segregates a single chromosome (1 -> 2) and then divides one cell into two daughters that each keep exactly one chromosome carrying its DNA -- a true partition, not a copy -- and keeps dividing 1 -> 2 -> 4 -> 8 under a capacity cap. A collectives rewrite (`build_fig10_biofilm`, `build_fig10_evolution`) grows a biofilm to carrying capacity then secretes ECM, and evolves a population in which a mutant lineage arises and sweeps the wildtype to extinction within a bounded population. Together these demonstrate the figure's core claim at the level of running topology: development and its neighbors (division, collective formation, evolution) are compositional rewrites that change the place graph itself.
These composites are deliberately DIDACTIC / toy-real: small, illustrative place graphs built to look like the figure and play forward through the process-bigraph engine, NOT calibrated to any biofilm, adhesion energetics, or ECM secretion literature. The rigorous spatial cousin -- a real CPM/metabolism realization of growth into a structured community -- is `development-and-evolution` in the `draft-to-living-cell` investigation; this study does not restate its numbers.
claim: The paper's §Development figure (Fig development) is executable, not merely drawn: running the `fig10-emergence` composite performs a genuine runtime place-graph rewrite that turns four free motile bacteria (top-level siblings) into a nested biofilm microcolony that then secretes an extracellular matrix -- "individual cells become part of a collective composite" (caption b) via "surface attachment, ECM secretion, growth of structured communities" (caption a). Over a deterministic 16-step run: all four free cells attach at once at t=6 (free 4 -> 0, biofilm-nested 0 -> 4) as a new `biofilm` collective node appears and the cells' place-graph depth increases from 1 to 2 and never reverts; ECM is absent until maturation and then accumulates to 3 nodes over t=12..14, only while the sessile community exists. This is a hierarchical reorganization -- a re-parenting into a collective with its own shared state -- not merely more cells. Two companion rewrites exercised by the same suite (cell-cycle division 1 -> 2 -> 4 -> 8 with true chromosome partition; biofilm-to-capacity + ECM, and a mutant lineage sweeping a wildtype population) confirm the same principle across the section's neighboring transformations. The composites are toy-real and uncalibrated; the calibrated spatial cousin is `development-and-evolution` in `draft-to-living-cell`.

variants.name: fig10-mechanistic
variants.rationale: Real-mechanism upgrade (scientific-review revision, Oct 2026). The baseline fig10-emergence reorganizes the place graph on a WALL CLOCK (attach_at/mature_at), so it shows the structure of the rewrite but not an emergent decision (the review's objection). This variant (BiofilmColony, handlers_fig10_mech.py) makes attachment EMERGE from spatial state: six motile cells on a 2-D box (lattice units) aggregate by LOCAL adhesion toward neighbours, and the biofilm forms only once a quorum sits within form_radius of the centroid for sustain_ticks consecutive ticks — a place-graph rewrite nesting the cells under a new biofilm node (identity + biomass preserved; the reparenting kept as a topology smoke test). Sessile cells secrete ECM that binds the community (cohesion = ECM/(ECM+k)); without ECM they spread back apart. Because the trigger is cluster geometry, formation TIME varies with adhesion and density — a wall clock cannot. Matched-null controls (adhesion off, ECM off — via epsilon) isolate each arm. The baseline is kept intact as the didactic smoke test.

key_assumptions: These fig-10 composites are DIDACTIC / toy-real: small, illustrative place graphs built to look like the figure and play forward through the process-bigraph engine, NOT calibrated to biofilm, adhesion, or ECM-secretion literature. `attach_at` (6.0), `mature_at` (12.0), `ecm_count` (3.0), the four founding cells, and the division/biofilm/evolution capacities are hand-picked, unitless model-time and count values chosen to make attach -> mature -> ECM legible within a short run.

Development is realized here as an EVENT-DRIVEN place-graph rewrite, not emergent self-assembly: the `BiofilmEmergence` process fires ATTACHMENT+AGGREGATION at a scheduled tick and MATURATION at a later scheduled tick. The timings are scripted (config `attach_at`/`mature_at`); what the composite demonstrates is the STRUCTURE of the reorganization (free siblings -> nested collective -> matrix-encased community), not an emergent decision about when to attach.

The `fig10-emergence` run is deterministic -- there is no RNG in the attachment, aggregation, or maturation rewrites -- so every count and timing (attach at t=6, ECM 1/2/3 at t=12/13/14, final 4 nested cells + 3 ECM) is an exact regression pin, reproduced byte-for-byte run to run, valid while the composite config is pinned.

Attachment is modeled as a hierarchical RE-PARENTING (the four cells leave the top level and become children of a new `biofilm` node), and cell identity/biomass is carried across; it is a topological reorganization of the place graph, not a physical/spatial aggregation with adhesion forces or diffusing signals. Signaling, morphogen gradients, and differentiation from the paper's broader §Development discussion are NOT modeled here.

The companion cell-cycle (`build_fig10_division`) and collectives (`build_fig10_biofilm`, `build_fig10_evolution`) rewrites exercised by the same test suite are likewise toy-real, scheduled rewrites (division at a cycle interval, biofilm growth every N ticks to a capacity, a mutation scheduled at a fixed tick that then sweeps) -- illustrative topology dynamics, not fitted growth, secretion, or selection rates.
acceptance_criteria: Before attachment, the four founding cells are free planktonic top-level siblings of the environment and no `biofilm` collective node exists.

Running the composite performs a genuine place-graph rewrite: at attachment all free cells leave the top level at once (free count -> 0) and become nested children of a new `biofilm` collective node (nested count -> all founders), and the cells never return to the top level -- a hierarchical reorganization (place-graph depth 1 -> 2), not relabelling or duplication.
The extracellular matrix appears only AFTER maturation (strictly after attachment) and only ever while the sessile community is present -- ECM secreted by a matured collective, not by free cells.

The companion cell-cycle rewrite genuinely partitions structure: a chromosome segregates 1 -> 2, then a cell divides into two daughters that each keep exactly one chromosome carrying its DNA, and the colony keeps dividing (2 -> 4 -> 8) under a capacity bound.

The companion collectives rewrites reorganize topology under bounds: a biofilm colonizes to carrying capacity then secretes ECM, and a mutant lineage arises and sweeps the wildtype to extinction within a bounded population.

units_and_time.time: 1 step = 1 unit of dimensionless model time (interval = 1.0); the baseline run is 16 such steps (17 emitted frames, t=0..16).
units_and_time.quantities: cell / ECM / chromosome / organism / mutant counts are integer place-graph node counts, not physical mass or cell numbers; biomass and dna values are dimensionless model quantities. attach_at (6.0), mature_at (12.0), ecm_count (3.0), and the companion cycle/grow intervals and capacities carry no calibrated physical unit.
units_and_time.note: No quantity here is calibrated to a named organism, biofilm, adhesion energetics, or ECM-secretion literature target.

findings.statement: Running the `fig10-emergence` composite performs a genuine runtime place-graph rewrite that realizes the paper's §Development figure: four free motile bacteria (top-level place-graph siblings) attach all at once into a single nested `biofilm` collective node -- the cells' depth increasing from 1 to 2 -- and never return to the top level. This is caption b's "hierarchical reorganization where individual cells become part of a collective composite," a re-parenting into a collective with its own shared state, not merely more cells. Confirmed deterministically: free 4 -> 0 and nested 0 -> 4 at t=6, a new biofilm node appearing exactly then, depth 1 -> 2 persisting for the rest of the run.

findings.statement: The matured sessile community secretes an extracellular matrix strictly after attachment -- caption a's "surface attachment, ECM secretion, growth of structured communities" in order. ECM is absent until maturation and then accumulates to 3 nodes, appearing only ever while the nested community is present (secreted by the collective, never by free cells). Confirmed deterministically: ECM 0 through t=11, then 1/2/3 at t=12/13/14, every ECM-bearing frame carrying 4 nested cells.

A cell-cycle rewrite segregates a chromosome (1 -> 2) then divides one cell into two daughters that each keep exactly one chromosome carrying its DNA (a true partition, not a copy), continuing 1 -> 2 -> 4 -> 8 under a capacity cap; a collectives rewrite grows a biofilm to carrying capacity then secretes ECM, and evolves a population in which a mutant lineage arises and sweeps the wildtype to extinction within a bounded population. findings.statement: The attachment rewrite is cell-CONSERVING and structure-preserving, not a copy or a relabelling. Over the deterministic 16-step run exactly four free top-level cells become exactly four biofilm-nested cells at t=6 -- none created, none dropped -- each cell's biomass is carried across the re-parenting unchanged (1.0 before -> 1.0 after), and the environment's `surface` node persists intact through all 17 emitted frames. Aggregation moves nodes into the new collective composite without duplicating or losing them: the hierarchical reorganization edits the place graph's topology while conserving its contents. Confirmed in-memory.

findings.statement: Biofilm formation is EMERGENT in the mechanistic variant, fixing the review's central objection. The baseline's four free cells reparenting at t=6 and ECM at t=12 is an ordered SCRIPTED rewrite on a wall clock — it demonstrates the structure of the reorganization, not an emergent decision. Here six motile cells aggregate by local adhesion and the biofilm forms only once a quorum sits in proximity for several sustained ticks, so the formation TIME varies with adhesion strength (t=7/6/5 for adhesion 0.25/0.35/0.55) and with initial density — behaviour a clock cannot produce. The reparenting itself (6 cells nested under a new biofilm node, identity + biomass preserved) is retained as a topology smoke test.

findings.statement: The variant distinguishes AGGREGATION, COLLECTIVE MAINTENANCE, and the (absent) true developmental change — honestly. Matched-null controls isolate the arms: without adhesion the cells never aggregate (no biofilm); with adhesion but without ECM they aggregate and form but do not persist (sessile cells spread back apart, cluster radius 3.0→11.3, cohesion→0), so ECM provides collective MAINTENANCE, not formation. The collective cohesion port is inert until the community organizes. Honest scope: this is spatial self-assembly + matrix-dependent persistence — it is NOT differentiation or true developmental change (no cell-type divergence, no morphogen patterning); those remain the calibrated cousin's domain.

findings.statement: Honest limits: the mechanistic biofilm is a reduced 2-D aggregation model in LATTICE units. Adhesion is a deterministic drift toward the neighbour centroid (not a stochastic bond-formation probability with measured affinities), ECM is a single well-mixed pool binding the whole community (not a diffusing, degrading spatial field with nutrient coupling), there is no flow, nutrient gradient, or growth/division during assembly, and every rate (adhesion, ecm_rate, decay, spread_rate) is didactic — not fitted to measured adhesion forces, ECM secretion/diffusion rates, or a named organism. It demonstrates that attachment CAN emerge from spatial state under test; it does not claim a calibrated biofilm.

conclusion:
## Claims
- The paper's §Development figure (Fig development) is executable: running the `fig10-emergence` composite performs a genuine runtime place-graph rewrite that turns four free motile bacteria (top-level siblings) into a nested biofilm microcolony (attach at t=6: free 4 -> 0, nested 0 -> 4, a new biofilm collective node, cell depth 1 -> 2 and never reverting) that then secretes an extracellular matrix (ECM 0 -> 1 -> 2 -> 3 over t=12..14, only while the sessile community exists). This is caption b's "hierarchical reorganization where individual cells become part of a collective composite" via caption a's "surface attachment, ECM secretion, growth of structured communities" -- a re-parenting into a collective, not merely more cells. Deterministic, exact, reproduced run to run.
- The same principle holds across the section's companion figures, exercised by the same fig-10 suite: a cell-cycle rewrite segregates a chromosome (1 -> 2) then divides a cell into two daughters that each keep one chromosome with its DNA (true partition), continuing 1 -> 2 -> 4 -> 8 under a capacity cap; a collectives rewrite grows a biofilm to capacity then secretes ECM, and evolves a population in which a mutant lineage sweeps the wildtype to extinction within a bound. Development, division, collective formation, and evolution are all compositional rewrites of the place graph.

## Evidence
- **FREE-CELLS-ATTACH-INTO-A-NESTED-BIOFILM** -- free 4 -> 0 at t=6, biofilm node holds all 4 nested
- **ATTACHMENT-NESTS-CELLS-ONE-LEVEL-DEEPER** -- cell place-graph depth 1 -> 2 at t=6, new collective node, never reverts
- **ECM-SECRETED-ONLY-AFTER-MATURATION** -- ECM 0 through t=11, then 1/2/3 at t=12/13/14, only while nested cells present
- **DIVISION-REWRITES-AND-PARTITIONS-THE-PLACE-GRAPH** -- chrom 1 -> 2 then 2 daughters each 1 chromosome dna==1.0, 1 -> 2 -> 4 -> 8, capacity caps
- **COLLECTIVES-COLONIZE-AND-A-LINEAGE-SWEEPS** -- biofilm 1 -> 5 then ECM; mutant arises, sweeps wildtype -> 0 within capacity 6

## Limitations
- Toy-real and uncalibrated: attach_at, mature_at, ecm_count, founder count, and the companion capacities are hand-picked unitless model-time/count values, not fitted to any biofilm, adhesion, or ECM-secretion data. The rigorous spatial cousin is `development-and-evolution` in the `draft-to-living-cell` investigation.
- The rewrites are event-driven at SCHEDULED ticks -- the composite demonstrates the STRUCTURE of the reorganization, not an emergent decision about when to attach or mature.
- Attachment is a topological re-parenting, not a physical/spatial aggregation; adhesion forces, diffusing signals, morphogen gradients, and differentiation from the paper's broader §Development discussion are not modeled.

## Next steps
- Compare against the spatial cousin `development-and-evolution` to contrast the toy-real place-graph rewrite with a calibrated CPM/metabolism realization of growth into a structured community.

diagnose: free cells never leave the top level or no biofilm node appears (the ATTACHMENT+AGGREGATION rewrite did not fire, or attach_at is beyond the run length)
ECM appears before or without attachment (the MATURATION rewrite is mis-ordered or ECM is secreted outside the collective)
cell depth does not increase 1 -> 2, or cells are copied rather than re-parented (the rewrite duplicates instead of moving nodes)
a daughter loses its chromosome/DNA, or the colony fails to keep dividing / exceeds capacity (the division partition or capacity cap is broken)
the mutant lineage fails to arise or sweep, or the population exceeds capacity (the evolution rewrite or its bound is broken)

limitations: These fig-10 composites are didactic / toy-real: small, illustrative place graphs built to look like the figure and play forward through the engine, NOT calibrated to biofilm, adhesion, or ECM-secretion literature. attach_at (6.0), mature_at (12.0), ecm_count (3.0), the four founding cells, and the companion capacities are hand-picked unitless model-time/count values chosen to make the attach -> mature -> ECM arc legible within a short run.

The rigorous spatial cousin is `development-and-evolution` in the `draft-to-living-cell` investigation -- a calibrated CPM/metabolism realization of growth into a structured community. This study does not restate that cousin's numbers as its own.

Development is realized as an event-driven place-graph rewrite fired at SCHEDULED ticks (config attach_at / mature_at), not emergent self-assembly: the composite demonstrates the STRUCTURE of the reorganization (free siblings -> nested collective -> matrix-encased community), not an emergent decision about when to attach or mature.

Attachment is a hierarchical re-parenting of the place graph (cells leave the top level and become children of a new biofilm node), not a physical/spatial aggregation with adhesion forces or diffusing signals. Signaling, morphogen gradients, and differentiation from the paper''s broader §Development discussion are not modeled here.

The companion cell-cycle, biofilm, and evolution rewrites exercised by the same suite are likewise toy-real scheduled rewrites (division at a cycle interval, biofilm growth every N ticks to a capacity, a mutation scheduled at a fixed tick that then sweeps) -- illustrative topology dynamics, not fitted growth, secretion, or selection rates.

Mechanistic variant (fig10-mechanistic) — scope and honest limits: it makes attachment EMERGE from spatial aggregation (fixing the baseline's scheduled trigger) and adds matched-null controls and identity-preserving reparenting, but it is a REDUCED 2-D aggregation model in LATTICE units. Adhesion is a deterministic centroid drift (not stochastic bond formation with measured affinities), ECM is a single well-mixed binding pool (not a diffusing/degrading spatial field coupled to nutrients), there is no flow, nutrient gradient, growth, or division during assembly, and all rates are didactic. It demonstrates emergent collective formation and matrix-dependent persistence under test — aggregation and collective maintenance — NOT differentiation or true developmental change, and is not calibrated to a named organism. The calibrated spatial cousin remains `development-and-evolution` in draft-to-living-cell.
falsifiability: Overturned if running the composite does not move all free cells out of the top level into a single nested biofilm node at attachment, if the cells' place-graph depth does not increase from 1 to 2 (or reverts), if the biofilm collective node is not newly created at attachment, if ECM appears before or without maturation or outside the collective, if any of these counts or timings fail to reproduce across repeated runs of the pinned deterministic composite, or if the companion division/biofilm/evolution rewrites fail to partition, colonize-then-secrete, or sweep within their bounds.
